newsitem.title: USA: Memphis, Tenn., airport mulls easement bonds.
newsitem.headline: Memphis, Tenn., airport mulls easement bonds.

text.p: Tennessee's Memphis-Shelby County Airport Authority has proposed an $18 million revenue bond issue to fund a potential settlement with neighbors who sued over airport noise and polluution, an airport official said Friday.

The proposal would settle a 1989 federal court lawsuit filed by residents who said noise and pollution from plane overflights had hurt property values and impaired quality of life following a major airport expansion.
Jerry McMichael, executive vice president of the airport authority, said he could not comment on specifics of the settlement offer.
But he said that if it is accepted, the bond issue would have to be approved by the tenant airlines and by the authority's board of commissioners.
"We would expect both these entitues would approve the sale," McMichael said.
There has been no decision on underwriters for the proposed issue, he said. The authority has about $470 million of airport revenue and special obligation bonds outstanding.
Quoting lawyers for the plaintiffs, the Commercial Appeal newspaper said the bond proceeds would be used to buy "aviation easements" giving planes the right to fly over residential areas.

The settlement would give about $1,500 each to the owners of 12,000 properties in the affected area. At least 95 percent of the owners would have to participate in order for the proposal to be accepted, the newspaper said.

The airport has spent $115 million of federal, local and state funds to buy 1,289 homes and four churches in the Whitehaven, Oakhaven, Southaven and Charjean communities since 1989 as part of a noise buyout program.
McMichael said it was impossible to predict when the case would be resolved if the settlement is rejected.
"It's been a very complicated suit. It could go for years. Somewhere along the line a judge could dismiss it. You just never know," he said.
